Subscription offers vs IAP product names vs listing promotional text

App Store Connect stores three different string families that US/EU indie teams often conflate. This page covers subscription offer display copy only — the promotional line buyers see when an offer is active:

  • Subscription product display name — the tier title on the purchase sheet (“Annual Pro”, “月度专业版”). Covered on our IAP localization guide — a different Connect row from offer strings.
  • Subscription offer display copy — the deal headline and description Apple attaches to an active offer: “Try free for 7 days”, “50% off your first year”, “Welcome back — 3 months for $0.99”, or offer-code redemption text. This page.
  • Listing promotional text — the 170-character field above the description on the product page, updatable without a new binary. Covered on our promotional text guide — not the subscribe-sheet offer line.

You can localize the product name and still leave every offer string English-only. Buyers then see a Chinese tier name with an English discount banner — a mismatch that reads like half-finished localization. See also China App Store still shows English when entire rows fall back.

Four offer types that need their own zh-Hans strings

Auto-renewable subscriptions in App Store Connect can carry multiple offer types. Each type exposes customer-facing display name and description fields per locale — including Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans):

  • Introductory offers — free trial, pay up front, or pay as you go for new subscribers. The line buyers see: “7 days free, then ¥68/month” or “First month free.”
  • Promotional offers — discounted pricing for existing or lapsed subscribers who meet eligibility. Copy like “Save 50% for 3 months” or “Limited-time renewal discount.”
  • Win-back offers — targeted re-engagement for churned subscribers. Banner text such as “We miss you — come back for 50% off” often stays English-only even when the tier name is localized.
  • Offer codes — custom or one-time-use codes with their own display name and description shown at redemption. “Holiday Special” and “Redeem 3 months half price” need zh-Hans equivalents separate from the base subscription strings.

Each offer record in Connect has localization rows distinct from the subscription product’s base display name. Empty zh-Hans offer rows fall back to English — which is the gap this page addresses.

Where subscription offer copy lives in App Store Connect

Open your app → Features → Subscriptions → select your subscription group → select a subscription product → Subscription Prices or Offers (labels vary by Connect version). For each introductory, promotional, win-back, or offer-code record, add or edit localization:

  • Offer display name — short headline on the subscribe sheet and subscription management UI when the offer is active
  • Offer description — clarifies duration, eligibility, or renewal terms in one or two lines
  • Offer-code customer-facing name — what redeemers see when entering or applying a code (separate from the internal reference name)

Verify current character limits in Connect before you save — Apple caps offer strings separately from IAP product display names. We deliver counted zh-Hans strings that fit the fields you paste into.

Why English-only offer lines hurt China storefront conversion

Western indie teams often localize the listing and even the subscription tier name, then ship offers configured once in English for the US storefront. On the China storefront the buyer flow looks like this:

  • Localized tier, English deal — “年度专业版” with “1 month free, then $9.99/month” — currency and duration habits feel foreign
  • Percent-off slogans without context — “Save 50%” with no Chinese explanation of which billing period qualifies
  • Win-back banner in English — lapsed zh-Hans users get a push or email in Chinese, tap through, and land on “Welcome back!” in English
  • Offer-code redemption mismatch — influencer posts a Chinese promo; redeem screen still shows “Spring Sale — 3 months half off”
  • Trial legalese tone — “Free for 7 days. Cancel anytime.” translated literally reads stiff; Chinese buyers expect concise renewal clarity

Clearer zh-Hans offer copy reduces confusion at subscribe time. It does not replace offer eligibility rules, pricing decisions, in-app paywall UI, or Apple’s review outcomes.

Introductory vs promotional vs win-back — copy differences

Each offer type answers a different buyer question. zh-Hans strings should match that intent:

  • Introductory — state trial length and what happens after: “免费试用 7 天，之后按月自动续费 ¥XX” not a vague “Try it free”
  • Promotional — name the discount window and who qualifies: “老用户专享：前 3 个月半价” not a generic “Limited offer”
  • Win-back — acknowledge lapse without guilt-tripping English idioms: “欢迎回来，续订享 3 个月优惠” beats “We miss you!”
  • Offer codes — tie the code name to the benefit in plain Chinese: “年终回馈：3 个月半价续订”

Align offer vocabulary with your localized IAP product display names — if the tier is “专业版”, offers should say “专业版” not reintroduce an English brand tier name.

Why machine-translated offer copy fails on the subscribe sheet

  • English duration patterns preserved — “1 month free” left half-English instead of “首月免费”
  • Percent symbols without billing context — “50% OFF” with no mention of which renewal cycle
  • US marketing idioms — “Best value”, “Most popular plan”, “Unlock savings” — that Chinese buyers read as ad fluff
  • Character overflow — long English descriptions pasted into short Connect offer fields truncate mid-word on device
  • Inconsistent trial language between offer description and In-App Event cards that reference the same promo

Machine translation is fine for internal drafts. Finished offer strings need idiomatic zh-Hans that states duration, scope, and renewal in plain language — while keeping your English product voice. AppLocale rewrites offer copy by hand; we do not deliver raw Google Translate or LLM output as finished strings.

What good zh-Hans subscription offer copy looks like

Offer lines appear for seconds on the subscribe sheet. Strong Chinese offer strings lead with the benefit and end with renewal clarity:

  • Display name: duration or discount headline — “首月免费”, “续订 3 个月半价”, “欢迎回来专享优惠”
  • Description: one line on eligibility and renewal — “新用户专享，到期后按标准价格自动续费”
  • Consistent tier terms — same “专业版 / 年度” vocabulary as your IAP product row
  • No unverifiable superlatives — scope and timing instead of “Best deal ever”

zh-Hans and en-US offer strings can differ in length and structure when the underlying deal is the same — avoid mirroring English comma-heavy marketing lines character-for-character.
